# The fundamental group of the circle

**Hatcher, Theorem 1.7 (page 29).** `π₁(S¹)` is infinite cyclic, generated by
the class of the loop `ω(s) = (cos 2πs, sin 2πs)` based at `(1, 0)`.

Equivalently, the [winding number](winding-number.md) is an isomorphism
`π₁(S¹, 1) ≅ ℤ`. Both directions are short once lifting is available.
Surjectivity: the path `ω̃ₙ(s) = ns` in `ℝ` runs from `0` to `n` and projects to
the loop `ωₙ(s) = (cos 2πns, sin 2πns)`, so `ωₙ` has winding number `n`.
Injectivity: if `f` has winding number `n`, then `f̃` and `ω̃ₙ` are paths in `ℝ`
with the same endpoints, hence homotopic by the linear homotopy
`(1 − t)f̃ + t ω̃ₙ`; composing that homotopy with `p` shows `f ≃ ωₙ`. So the
class of `f` is determined by its winding number.

This is the project's main target. Nothing in the pinned Mathlib computes
`π₁` of the circle, although every ingredient above is present.

Intended artifact: `Hatcher.Circle.fundamentalGroupEquivInt` in
`Hatcher/Circle/FundamentalGroup.lean`, stated as a `MulEquiv` onto
`Multiplicative ℤ`.
